summary: Cheap to build and $0 to run, but demand for per-PR cost is only inferred and free tools (ccusage, claude-burn-rate) already cover most of it. No evidence anyone would pay.

demand.evidence: Adjacent pain only (Anthropic cost docs, blogs, anecdotes); RESEARCH.md found no thread asking for per-PR cost; no one has paid or asked for it.

statusQuo.evidence: /usage, ccusage and claude-burn-rate (per-branch) already exist and are free; the gap is only posting to the PR.

specificity.evidence: Target is 'small-team dev/lead on metered billing', a category; no named person; subscription users aren't billed per token.

wedge.evidence: Branch receipt CLI is a weekend build, but its output overlaps claude-burn-rate; the PR comment is the true differentiator.

futureFit.evidence: Rising-tide argument; Anthropic or ccusage can add per-PR cost natively; a feature rather than a product.

premises: Teams care about cost per PR, not per day or user (unsupported)
Claude Code logs reliably record gitBranch and cwd (unverified)
Developers will publish spend on PRs (doubtful for public repos)
Enough small teams are on metered billing (partly supported)
Someone will pay for it (unsupported; free-tool market)
alternatives: Minimal: a script or ccusage wrapper that prints a PR-ready markdown block by branch; open source it and measure stars
Ideal: GitHub Action plus exported JSON, multi-agent, cost-per-merged-PR trends (hosted, conflicts with $0)
Lateral: contribute branch/PR-comment support to ccusage or claude-burn-rate
No David repo overlaps (pr-split and RepoHQ do not do cost attribution), so there is nothing to extend
wedge: prreceipt comment: one idempotent PR comment with an aggregate cost receipt from local Claude Code logs

feasibility.notes: TypeScript + Node CLI with fixture tests. One test: fixture of 3 messages at 1,000 in / 500 out at $3/$15 per M yields $0.0315 and 4,500 tokens, plus a real-logs check within 5% of ccusage; verify gitBranch is present on entries.

risks: Free incumbents and Anthropic could ship this natively
No clear monetization for a local open-source CLI
Branch metadata gaps (worktrees, renames) hurt trust
Subscription users see only an API-equivalent estimate
Privacy concerns about spend on public PRs
killCriteria: Drop if fewer than 3 people unprompted ask for per-PR cost, if branch attribution covers under 80% of real sessions, or if ccusage/claude-burn-rate ships PR comments.
